## Highlights

- **The backend resolves external names again when Docker's resolver is a private address.** The backend's egress fence (`install_ssrf_firewall` in the platform image's entrypoint) rejected every private range except the container's own subnets. Docker's embedded resolver forwards external names to the daemon's DNS servers from inside the container, so where that server is a private address, such as an Incus bridge gateway, every external name failed with `getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN`: adding a model provider, reading its catalog and fetching a video link all failed, while names on the compose network still resolved. The fence now accepts DNS (udp and tcp port 53, nothing else) to each upstream resolver the container is configured with, ahead of the private-range rejects, and logs them at start. Resolvers that Docker dials from the host open nothing, and a container whose resolvers cannot be read keeps the fence with a warning. The Kubernetes install page describes the DNS pass ([#5491](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5491)).
- **A custom provider's models are listed with the key you entered.** Every model listing sent the organization's saved default credential, so the add dialog of a custom provider behind a key-gated gateway never listed its models, and a non-default credential's **Check models** used the default key. The add and edit dialogs gain **List models**, which lists the provider's models with the key typed in the dialog or with the selected saved credential, enabled or not, and fills the model allowlist from the result. The key goes only to the provider's own models endpoint, in the request body, and is never cached, logged or returned. A remembered refusal now applies to the key that was refused alone, and a listing that needs a key (`PROVIDER_CATALOG_KEY_REQUIRED`) is told apart from one whose key was refused (`PROVIDER_CATALOG_KEY_REFUSED`) ([#5497](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5497)).
- **OpenRouter embeddings no longer fail at random.** OpenRouter serves Qwen3 Embedding 8B from three endpoints, and one of them accepts only fixed vector widths, not the 1536 that Tale asks for. Requests routed there were refused or came back at a width Tale could not store. Tale now tells OpenRouter to skip the endpoints that cannot serve the organization's stored width, so organizations already at 1536 keep their index and need no re-index. The data-residency docs explain the routing ([#5493](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5493)).
- **Video links fail over when YouTube walls the address.** YouTube's session wall ("This content isn't available") was read as a removed video, and a refused player response ("Failed to extract any player response") as a transient error that was retried from the same address. The first now reads as a rate limit and the second as a bot wall: a run through the outbound proxies moves on to the next proxy, the walled session is marked blocked, and the user sees the rate-limit or blocked-access reason instead of "video gone" ([#5501](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5501), [#5502](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5502)).

## Upgrade notes

- **Platform:** run the `0.5.108` images and upgrade the `tale` CLI with them. This release adds no database migration and does not change the API contract version. No configuration change is needed.
- **If you turned the egress fence off** with `TALE_SKIP_SSRF_FIREWALL=1` because external names did not resolve, turn it back on with this release: set it to `0`, deploy, and check that the backend logs the resolvers it allows. A stack's `.env` keeps a key that was set before, so removing the variable alone leaves the fence off.
- **OpenRouter embeddings:** the routing applies to new embedding requests at once. Stored vectors and the organization's width do not change.
